stages.label: Study
stages.description: A US bachelor’s degree typically takes four years.

stages.label: Post-study work visa
stages.description: Optional Practical Training (OPT) gives 12 months of work after graduation, up to 36 months for STEM degrees. Staying longer means winning the annual H-1B visa lottery.

stages.label: PR process
stages.description: There is no direct study-to-residence route. After H-1B an employer-sponsored green card runs about 3 to 4 years for most nationalities, but Indian and Chinese citizens face waits of a decade or more under per-country caps.

stages.label: Citizenship
stages.description: Green-card holders can apply for naturalization after five years of permanent residence.

sources.name: USCIS: Optional Practical Training (OPT) for F-1 students

stages.label: Study
stages.description: A UK bachelor’s degree is typically three years (four in Scotland).

stages.label: Post-study work visa
stages.description: The Graduate Route lets you stay two years to work or job-hunt at any skill level, but this time does not count toward settlement.

stages.label: PR process
stages.description: Settlement (Indefinite Leave to Remain) needs five continuous years on a Skilled Worker visa, so you must switch routes. The 2025 white paper proposed extending this qualifying period to ten years.

stages.label: Citizenship
stages.description: You can usually apply for British citizenship about 12 months after gaining ILR.

sources.name: GOV.UK: Indefinite leave to remain (Skilled Worker)

stages.label: Study
stages.description: A Canadian bachelor's degree typically runs four years. Graduating from a program this length earns a post-graduation work permit (PGWP) valid for up to three years.

stages.label: Post-study work visa
stages.description: Express Entry's Canadian Experience Class needs 12 months of skilled Canadian work, gained on the PGWP, before you can apply for permanent residence.

stages.label: PR process
stages.description: After the work requirement is met, an Express Entry profile usually leads to an invitation and PR being granted within about a year. This duration is a representative estimate.

stages.label: Citizenship
stages.description: Citizenship needs 1,095 days (three years) of physical presence in the five years before applying. Time spent in Canada on the PGWP before PR counts as a half day each, up to 365 days.

stages.label: Study
stages.description: An Australian bachelor’s degree is typically three years.

stages.label: Post-study work visa
stages.description: The Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485) gives bachelor’s graduates two years of post-study work rights (longer for research degrees).

stages.label: PR process
stages.description: Permanent residence is points-based skilled migration, with no lottery but rising thresholds and occupation lists. Many use the 485 years to build points and secure state nomination.

stages.label: Citizenship
stages.description: Citizenship needs four years of lawful residence including the final 12 months as a permanent resident.

sources.name: Department of Home Affairs: Temporary Graduate visa (485)
Department of Home Affairs: Become an Australian citizen

stages.label: Study
stages.description: A German bachelor’s degree usually takes three years, taught in German or, increasingly, in English.

stages.label: Post-study work visa
stages.description: Graduates get an 18-month residence permit (via the Opportunity Card / Chancenkarte route) to find qualified work.

stages.label: PR process
stages.description: With an EU Blue Card and B1 German you can reach a settlement permit in as little as 21 to 33 months; without German it is the standard five years.

stages.label: Citizenship
stages.description: Since the 2024 reform, citizenship is possible after five years (three with strong integration), and dual nationality is now allowed.

sources.name: Make it in Germany: after your studies

stages.label: Study
stages.description: An Irish honours bachelor’s degree usually takes three to four years.

stages.label: Post-study work visa
stages.description: The Third Level Graduate Scheme (Stamp 1G) gives bachelor’s graduates 12 months to find work (24 months for a master’s).

stages.label: PR process
stages.description: You switch to an employment permit, then to long-term residence (Stamp 4). Critical Skills permit holders can reach Stamp 4 in about 21 months; the general route takes far longer.

stages.label: Citizenship
stages.description: Naturalisation needs five years of reckonable residence in the past nine, with the final year continuous.

sources.name: gov.ie: becoming an Irish citizen through naturalisation

stages.label: Study
stages.description: A Dutch research-university bachelor’s is typically three years (four at universities of applied sciences), and many programs are taught in English.

stages.label: Post-study work visa
stages.description: The orientation year (zoekjaar) lets graduates work any job for 12 months with no permit or salary threshold while job-hunting.

stages.label: PR process
stages.description: Study and orientation years count toward permanent residence, which needs five continuous years of legal residence plus the civic integration exam.

stages.label: Citizenship
stages.description: Citizenship also needs five years’ residence and the integration exam, so it arrives close behind permanent residence.
